newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes quiet with slightly weaker tone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes quiet with slightly weaker tone.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes started Thursday in a quiet mood, pacing ahead of Friday's pipeline scheduling for May crude barrels.

Traders said finding confirmation for trades was a chore, with talk floating around the market instead of deals. Price differentials for sweet and sour grades have fluctuated widely, but the general consensus viewed the market as weaker.

May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged 10-15 cents higher than June WTI/Cushing, though the roll was heard as wide as 30 cts over the second month. May WTI was around $19.85-90 a barrel, some 20 cts stronger than late Wednesday.
